intro: San José rewards visitors with lively markets, museums and easy escapes to volcanoes and cloud forests. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; buses cover the city and country from several downtown terminals.
City buses are cheap, about ₡500 per ride, with no transfers or day passes.
Use the Moovit app for bus routes and schedules.
Taxis should use a meter but often don't; agree the price first.
Uber and DiDi work well in the city, though Uber is technically illegal.
Driving is slow and confusing; walking is fine downtown but bike lanes are limited.

basilica.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Angels
basilica.landmark: Basilica of Our Lady of the Angels
basilica.hours: Daily roughly 06:00–18:00 · check mass times before you go
basilica.tip: Visit early morning to see pilgrims arrive, and walk the small museum and grotto behind the church.

gallo-pinto.name: Costa Rican Gallo Pinto
gallo-pinto.hours: Served mostly at breakfast · sodas open roughly 07:00–15:00
gallo-pinto.tip: Try it at a local 'soda' with Salsa Lizano and a coffee; it is rice and beans, not a single dish.

parque-diversiones.name: Parque de Diversiones Dr. Roberto Ortiz Brenes
parque-diversiones.landmark: Parque de Diversiones Dr. Roberto Ortiz Brenes
parque-diversiones.price_text: Paid entry and ride tickets · check current prices on the day
parque-diversiones.hours: Mostly weekends and holidays · confirm opening days before you go
parque-diversiones.tip: Good for families with kids; check the calendar first because it is not open every weekday.

mercado-central.name: Mercado Central
mercado-central.tip: Come hungry and try a 'casado' at one of the small lunch counters inside.

teatro-nacional.name: Teatro Nacional de Costa Rica
teatro-nacional.price_text: Small entry fee for the building tour · check on the day
teatro-nacional.hours: Roughly Mon–Sat daytime · confirm before visiting
teatro-nacional.tip: Step inside the lobby even briefly for the painted ceiling and marble staircase.

precolumbian.name: Museo del Oro Precolombino
precolumbian.price_text: Paid entry · check current price on the day
precolumbian.tip: The underground vault setting is as striking as the gold pieces; allow an hour.

jade-museum.name: Museo del Jade
jade-museum.price_text: Paid entry · check current price on the day
jade-museum.tip: Modern building with a strong collection; a good rainy-afternoon stop.

avenida-central.name: Avenida Central pedestrian walk
avenida-central.tip: Walk it end to end for street life and shops, but keep your phone out of sight and watch your bag.

barrio-amon.name: Barrio Amón heritage walk
barrio-amon.tip: Look up at the old wooden mansions; go in daylight and stay on the main streets.

barrio-escalante.name: Barrio Escalante food and café stroll
barrio-escalante.price_text: Free to walk · meals and coffee vary widely
barrio-escalante.hours: Cafés daytime · restaurants into the evening
barrio-escalante.tip: Come for lunch or dinner and pick a side street off Calle 33 for the best café density.

san-pedro.name: San Pedro and University of Costa Rica area
san-pedro.tip: Student neighbourhood with cheap eats and bookshops; go in daylight.

la-sabana.name: Parque Metropolitano La Sabana
la-sabana.tip: Big green lung with a lake and running paths; go in daylight and keep valuables close.

museo-nacional.name: Museo Nacional de Costa Rica
museo-nacional.price_text: Paid entry · check current price on the day
museo-nacional.tip: The old fort building and butterfly garden are the highlights.

cafe-oro.name: Café Oro coffee tasting
cafe-oro.price_text: Small tasting fee · check on the day
cafe-oro.tip: Short intro to Costa Rican coffee if you have no time for a coffee farm tour.

city-tour.name: San José walking tour
city-tour.price_text: Tip-based or paid · varies by operator
city-tour.tip: A guide helps you read the downtown safely and quickly; book a day ahead.

mercado-borbon.name: Mercado Borbón
mercado-borbon.tip: Less polished than Mercado Central and more local; good for fruit and a quick bite.

morazan.name: Parque Morazán
morazan.tip: Small plaza with the old railway station nearby; a quick photo stop in daylight.

art-museum.name: Museo de Arte Costarricense
art-museum.price_text: Often free or low-cost · check on the day
art-museum.tip: The gold-leaf mural room is the reason to come; it sits at the edge of La Sabana.

insect-museum.name: Museo de Insectos, University of Costa Rica
insect-museum.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
insect-museum.tip: Quirky and cheap; good with kids and a short stop in San Pedro.

escalante-night.name: Barrio Escalante evening bar and restaurant walk
escalante-night.price_text: Free to walk · dinner and drinks vary
escalante-night.tip: Book dinner ahead on weekends; take a taxi back after dark.

spirogyra.name: Butterfly garden at Spirogyra
spirogyra.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
spirogyra.tip: A calm green break in Barrio Escalante; best in the morning when butterflies are active.

mercado-escalante.name: Escalante farmers market (weekend)
mercado-escalante.price_text: Free to enter · pay per item
mercado-escalante.tip: Go early for fruit and coffee; it is small and gets busy.

gold-museum-2.name: Plaza de la Cultura
gold-museum-2.tip: Central meeting point above the gold museum; use it as a downtown landmark to orient yourself.

catedral.name: Catedral Metropolitana
catedral.tip: Quick look at the neoclassical interior; dress modestly.

stays.why: Walk to the National Theatre, museums and markets. Busy and basic by night; keep valuables close.
Quiet old quarter of colonial houses and small hotels, a short walk from downtown sights.
Best food and nightlife strip; leafy streets and boutique hotels. Good for evenings.
University district near the museums and San Pedro Mall; cheaper and local, a short bus or taxi from the centre.

food: Eat at a soda (small local diner): casado (rice, beans, plantain, meat) is a filling lunch, often ₡3,000–6,000.
Mercado Central downtown: fruit, coffee and cheap stalls; go before midday.
Barrio Escalante has the widest restaurant choice; book on weekend evenings.
Try gallo pinto at breakfast and fresh tropical fruit; coffee is a local point of pride.
Tap water is generally safe in the city; check on the day outside it.
more_time: Add a day trip to a coffee farm or Poás or Irazú volcano; tours leave early, check on the day for closures.
Swap a city afternoon for the Museo del Oro and Museo Nacional, both downtown.
Take a bus to Cartago or the Orosi Valley for colonial history and cooler air.
